covers: Wall Street's Monday 26 October close, the JSE's Monday close, and Asian and overnight trading to 06:20 SAST on Tuesday 27 October 2026
headline: Asian chip stocks jump and US futures edge up as the Fed's two-day meeting starts; oil slips for a second day on Iran mediation, and Moody's is seen as the agency most likely to upgrade South Africa
summary: The JSE All Share closed up about 1.0% at 109,130 on Monday (Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 26 Oct) despite Brazil's crash, and Business Day reports that Moody's could upgrade South Africa from Ba2 within about a year, with Moody's and S&P both reviewing on 27 November; the rand was near R16.64/$ early on Tuesday (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct). Wall Street closed higher on Monday (S&P 500 +0.70% at 7,676.77) and in Asia the Nikkei rose 1.9% and the KOSPI more than 4% on chip stocks, with Nasdaq futures up 0.4% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct). Brent eased about 0.7% to near $115 a barrel as talks with Iran continue, and gold was little changed near $4,010 an ounce ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision (Investing.com; Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct).

items.title: Israel votes today in an election that decides Netanyahu's future
items.summary: Israelis elect the 26th Knesset on Tuesday 27 October; most polling stations are open from 7am to 10pm local time. A government needs 61 of 120 seats, and polls show neither Netanyahu's bloc nor the opposition clearly reaching that number (Al Jazeera, 20 Oct). Why it matters: the result could shape Israel's role in the wider Gulf conflict, which is keeping oil above $100 a barrel.

items.title: Oil falls for a second day as Iran talks ease fears of a wider war
items.summary: At 00:10 GMT on Tuesday Brent December futures were down 0.6% at $115.15 a barrel and WTI down 0.5% at $105.25 (Investing.com, 27 Oct); Reuters later had Brent down 0.7% at $114.95 (Business Recorder, 27 Oct). Talks involve Iran, Saudi Arabia, Turkey and Pakistan, with Qatar also engaging with Tehran. Supply risks remain: the Houthis said on Monday they attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia's East-West pipeline and Riyadh airport, which Saudi Arabia had not confirmed, and Tehran wants the US blockade of its ports lifted as part of any deal (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: Wall Street closed higher on Monday; futures edge up as the Fed meets
items.summary: On Monday the S&P 500 closed at 7,676.77, the Nasdaq at 26,169.38 and the Dow at 52,361.58 (Reuters via Business Recorder, 26 Oct close); the S&P gained 0.70% on the day (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct). US chip stocks rose 2.8% and Nasdaq futures were up 0.4% in Asian hours on Tuesday; the 10-year Treasury yield was steady at 4.992% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct). The Fed's two-day meeting starts today; its decision is on Wednesday at 20:00 SAST and markets price only about a 10% chance of a hike this week (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: Asia: Nikkei up 1.9%, KOSPI up more than 4% as chip stocks rally
items.summary: On Tuesday morning the Nikkei was up 1.9%, South Korea's KOSPI more than 4% higher in early trade and MSCI's Asia-Pacific index outside Japan up 1.2%, after a large AI start-up filed for a Nasdaq listing. European stock futures were down 0.23% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct).

items.title: China's industrial profits rise 14.4% in September
items.summary: Profits at China's industrial firms rose 14.4% from a year earlier in September, the fastest pace since June, led by AI-related industries, while consumer-facing sectors lagged (National Bureau of Statistics via Investing.com, 27 Oct). Why it matters: China is the biggest buyer of South Africa's metals.

items.title: Results today: Visa after the close, Coca-Cola before the open
items.summary: Coca-Cola reports before the US open and Visa after the close on Tuesday 27 October; HSBC also reports today (Nasdaq earnings calendar, 26 Oct). Microsoft and Alphabet follow on Wednesday and Amazon on Thursday.

items.title: Moody's seen as most likely to upgrade South Africa, possibly within a year
items.summary: After Moody's called the medium-term budget 'credit positive', Business Day reports an upgrade from Ba2 (positive outlook since May) could come within about a year. Bank of America sees Moody's as the most likely agency to act, possibly to Ba1, and calls an S&P move to BB+ 'a closer call'; Investec's Annabel Bishop expects a Moody's upgrade in about 18 months, and Treasury says Moody's and S&P could upgrade within 12 to 18 months. Moody's and S&P review South Africa on 27 November and Fitch on 11 December. Moody's says a track record of fiscal delivery still has to be built (Business Day, 27 Oct). No rating action has been announced.

items.title: JSE shrugs off Brazil's crash; rand near R16.64/$
items.summary: The JSE All Share closed at 109,130.32 on Monday, up about 1.0% from Friday's 108,020.10, and the Top 40 at 100,977.01, up about 1.0% (Yahoo Finance via LRC Market Dashboard, 26 Oct). Brazil's Ibovespa closed down 13.88% at 176,608 and the dollar rose about 8.4% to near R$5.41 after Lula's re-election (Rio Times, 26 Oct). The rand was at 16.6371 to the dollar early on Tuesday, against 16.6125 on Monday morning (Yahoo Finance, 27 Oct; Reuters via Channel Africa, 26 Oct).
items.source: Rio Times; Channel Africa (Reuters); Yahoo Finance

items.title: Gold little changed near $4,010 ahead of the Fed
items.summary: At 00:53 GMT on Tuesday spot gold was down 0.2% at $4,010.39 an ounce and US gold futures down 0.3% at $4,023.57; silver was near $53.96, platinum down 0.1% at $1,529.27 and palladium up 0.1% at $1,046.65. The dollar index was at 102.04. High energy prices keep alive bets on a Fed hike before year-end (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: Dollar firm; yen weaker before Bank of Japan decision
items.summary: The dollar index was at 102.05 (+0.09%), the yen at 157.73 per dollar, EUR/USD at 1.1172 and GBP/USD at 1.3342 on Tuesday morning in Asia. The Bank of Japan is expected to hold at 1.25% on Friday (Investing.com, 27 Oct).

items.title: META: shares flat after the $35 billion share sale
items.summary: Meta closed at $642.70 on Monday, roughly unchanged on the day (LRC Stock Scanner, 26 Oct close), after launching $22.5 billion of common stock and $12.5 billion of mandatory convertible preferred, with up to $60 billion more planned from 2027 (TIKR, 26 Oct). Pricing of the offering is still to come. META is a BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.

items.title: NVIDIA: Asian chip rally follows Monday's 2.4% gain
items.summary: NVIDIA closed up 2.39% at $216.00 on Monday (Yahoo Finance, 26 Oct), and chip stocks extended gains in Asia on Tuesday, with the KOSPI up more than 4% (Reuters via Business Recorder, 27 Oct). Results are due on 17 November. NVDA is a BUY on the LRC Stock Scanner; rating unchanged.
